user.title: Set up Fetch Latest File
user.description: This integration allows you to fetch the most recently modified files from a directory based on filename patterns, extensions, and minimum file size. Results are reported by actual file extension.

abort.single_instance_allowed: Only a single instance of this integration is allowed.

init.title: Fetch Latest File Options
init.description: Configure cleanup behavior for target_id results

data.max_target_ids: Maximum number of target_ids to keep (1-100)

fetch.name: Fetch latest file
fetch.description: Fetches the most recent file that starts with the given filename in the specified directory, plus the latest match for each file extension. Optionally, filter by file extension and/or minimum file size.

directory.name: Directory
directory.description: The directory to search for files. The search is recursive and includes subdirectories.

filename.name: File name prefix
filename.description: The beginning of the name of the file to fetch. Case-insensitive.

extension.name: Extension
extension.description: The file extension(s) to search for. Can be a single extension or a list of extensions. Do not include the dot. Results are keyed by actual extension, such as jpg or mp4. Reserved result keys are prefixed with ext_.

min_size.name: Minimum file size
min_size.description: The minimum size of the file to fetch. Specify as a string with a unit: B (bytes), K (kilobytes), M (megabytes), or G (gigabytes).

target_id.name: Target ID
target_id.description: A unique identifier for this fetch operation. Service calls with different target_id values can run in parallel, while calls with the same target_id will execute sequentially to prevent conflicts. If not specified, uses 'default'.
